Instructions: This tutorial will teach the basics of developing your economy. You start with a Civic Center and a couple units in Village Phase; your goal is to develop and expand, evolving to Town Phase and City Phase.
Toggle fullscreen with Alt+Enter; zoom with the mouse wheel; move the camera with the arrow keys.
To start off, select your building, the Civic Center, by clicking on it. A selection ring in your player color will be displayed.
With the Civic Center selected, the production panel appears at the lower right. Available actions are unmasked; gray = not unlocked; red = insufficient resources. Hover icons for tooltips.
The top row trains units; the bottom rows research technologies. The II icon advances to Town Phase — it requires more structures plus food and wood.
Two main starting unit types: Civilians (pure economy) and Citizen Soldiers (workers that can fight). Civilians and Infantry gather all land resources; Cavalry can only gather meat from animals.
Rule of thumb: left-click selects; right-click with a selection issues an order (gather, build, fight…).

Food and wood matter most early. Civilians gather vegetables fastest. Select all your Civilians (drag a rectangle / click then Shift+click / double-click for same-type) and right-click the berries southeast of the Civic Center.
Now gather wood with your Infantry Citizen Soldiers: select them and right-click the nearest tree.
Cavalry Citizen Soldiers are good hunters. Select your Cavalry and order it to slaughter the chickens around your Civic Center.
Set a rally point so newly trained units go straight to work: select the Civic Center and right-click a tree south of it.
Rally points show as a small flag at the end of the blue line.

On.Warn: Select the Civic Center, then right-click a tree (cursor turns into a wood icon).

Instructions: Train more units: with the Civic Center selected, hold the batch-train key and click the second unit icon (Hoplites) to train five at once — cheaper than five single clicks.

On.WarnOnCount: Hold the batch hotkey while clicking to train several units.
On.WarnOnTemplate: The second icon trains the Hoplites.

Instructions: Wait for the units to be trained.
Watch the top-left resource counters: resources only count once workers deposit them at the Civic Center or another dropsite — minimize the walk distance for efficiency.

New units gather wood automatically, but the walk back is long. Build a Storehouse (wood/stone/metal dropsite) near the trees: select your five Citizen Soldiers, click the Storehouse icon, and place it by the trees.
Invalid (obstructed) spots show the building preview in red.
The selected Citizens start constructing automatically once the foundation is placed.
Builders now gather wood automatically. We have enough woodcutters — remove the rally point: right-click on the selected Civic Center (the flag icon shows crossed out).
Train Civilians for more food: select the Civic Center, hold the batch key, and click the Civilian icon to train five.

On.WarnOnCount: Hold the batch hotkey and click to train several units.
On.WarnOnTemplate: The first icon trains the Civilians.

Instructions: The units will be ready soon.
Watch the population counter (fifth item top-left): current population (including units in training) vs limit, which your structures set.
Near the population cap you must raise it with new structures — the House is cheapest.
Let's build several Houses in a row.

Select two newly-trained Civilians and build Houses east of the Civic Center: click the House icon, then hold the queue key while clicking several spots — units work through queued orders in order. Press Escape to drop the House cursor.
Reminder: click the first Civilian, then hold the add key and click the second.
Berries are finite — Fields give unlimited food but gather slower.
First build a Farmstead (a food dropsite) to minimize the walk.

Select the three remaining idle Civilians and build a Farmstead in the open area west of the Civic Center.
Leave room for Fields around it. Goats to the west can improve food income if hunted.
Tip: hold the idle-only key while drag-selecting to pick just the idle units.
Finished Farmstead builders will seek the goats automatically.
House builders idle once done — wait for them to finish both Houses.
With both Houses up, select your two Civilians and build a Field as close as possible to the Farmstead (it accepts all food).
Field builders will gather it automatically once done.
The cavalry should be done with the chickens — take it south past the Civic Center to the lake and right-click a camel to hunt.
Up to five Workers per Field. Set the Civic Center rally point on the Field: new Workers will help build it, then gather it.

On.Warn: Select the Civic Center and right-click on the Field.

Instructions: Click the Civilian icon three times to train three more farmers.

On.WarnOnCount: Click without the batch key to train a single unit.

Instructions: Gather rates improve with technologies. Select the Farmstead: its production panel lists researchable technologies — hover for costs/effects and pick one.
Prepare for Town Phase: hover its icon in the Civic Center panel to see what's missing.
Resources suffice but a structure is missing — and defense never hurts. Select four soldiers and build a Barracks near the Civic Center.
While the Barracks builds, rally two more builders onto its foundation (right-click it; hammer cursor) and train two more Hoplites.
You can now research Town Phase: select the Civic Center and click the technology icon.
If the icon shows red, wait for your workers to gather the missing resources.
Later phases need stone and metal for bigger structures and better soldiers.
While researching, send half your idle Citizen Soldiers to the stone quarry and half to the metal mine west of the Civic Center.
Soldiers carrying wood would lose it when switching resources — queue orders: hold the queue key, right-click the Civic Center to deposit, then right-click the quarry.
Repeat with the remaining soldiers and the metal mine.
This is the end of the walkthrough. You now know the basics of setting up your economy.
